events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
NS-0 routes this case: the driver cancelled and asserted a rider no-show, so the fee stands or falls under NS-1/NS-2 [F3][F12][NS-0]. The driver did tap "I'm Here" at 08:48:15, so NS-1(i) is met [F5][NS-1].

NS-1(ii) fails. The driver tapped while 350 m from the pickup point, his closest approach all trip was 288 m, he never entered the 200 m arrival radius, and the platform never recorded an arrival [F5][F1][F4][NS-1]. NS-1(iii) fails too: his stationarity of 4 min 0 s ran 08:47:55-08:51:55 at a point 350 m from pickup, and he spent 0 s continuously within the radius after the tap, so the "waited at the pickup point" element is not established by duration alone [F2][F5][NS-1]. Duration without location is not waiting at the pickup point.

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the gps record and by driver_arrived_at being null, so it cannot sustain the fee [F12][F1][F4][F5][NS-1]. The chat does not rescue him: his 08:48 "come out" message offers a car description, not a verified pickup location, and the rider replied at 08:49 that she was at the pickup point and saw no car [F8][F9][NS-1]. No traffic incident, speed-band record or weather condition is on the record to explain the shortfall, and none is claimed [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

Because NS-1(i)-(iii) are not all satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full: the fee on record is $6.61 and surge was 1.0x [F3][F6][F7][NS-2]. This is a single flat cancellation fee, not a metered-distance computation, so the amount is the recorded fee $6.61 [F6].

Separately, the driver tapped "I'm Here" while gps placed him outside the pickup radius, which is the false-arrival-tap limb of NS-2 and attracts an account flag [F5][F1][NS-2]. what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the tap), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: GPS shows his closest approach was 288 m at 08:47:45 and he never came within 200 m, and he then sat stationary 350 m away from 08:47:55 to 08:51:55.

Requirement (ii) of NS-1 fails: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:48:15 while he was 350 m from the pickup point, and the platform never recorded him arriving (driver_arrived_at is null); he stayed within 200 m of the pickup for 0 seconds.

Requirement (iii) of NS-1 also fails in substance: any waiting time that could count can only be the 4 minutes spent 350 m away from the pickup point, i.e. not waiting at the pickup point at all (0 s within 200 m).

The driver's own chat message confirms he was not at the pickup point he was told to come to: the rider said at 08:49 "I'm at the pickup point and I don't see any car", and the driver never gave a location matching the pickup point, consistent with the GPS record of 288 m minimum distance.

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the system records (never within 200 m, 0 s inside 200 m, no recorded arrival), so under the system-records-prevail rule it cannot support the no-show fee.
Because NS-1 (i)-(iii) are not all satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider; the fee charged is on record as $6.61 and no surge applied.

A flag_account against the driver is warranted: he pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 350 m from the pickup point and never inside the 200 m arrival radius, which Ryde treats as abuse of the arrival/waiting button; his profile also shows a prior upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days.
Nothing in the traffic or weather records excuses the driver's failure to reach the pickup point: no incidents, no speed bands and fair weather were recorded during the trip window.

There is no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in this record — the messages are ordinary and the rider merely asks where the car is — so the case can be decided automatically rather than escalated on safety grounds.

weaknesses: The driver did press "I'm Here" (F5) and did wait 4 minutes (F2), so he will argue the substance of NS-1 was met and only the geofence reading is imperfect; the 200 m radius itself is a data-layer parameter Ryde has not published (gap G2), which he may attack.

His written statement (F12) asserts he waited at the pickup point; although it is contradicted by the GPS record (F1, F4, F5), it is the only account on his side and the judge must weigh the conflict.
The rider's own message (F9) says she was at the pickup point but the record contains no independent GPS fix of the rider's position, so her presence rests on the chat alone.
F17 shows the driver's prior upheld dispute is only one no-show case, so the flag_account request rests on a thin 'repeated' pattern and profile facts cannot decide the case by themselves.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here" before cancelling, at 08:48:15, so the no-show procedure under NS-1 was at least initiated in the app.
The driver's stationary wait was 4 min 0 s (08:47:55–08:51:55), which exceeds the 3-minute threshold on its face, so the duration element of NS-1(iii) is met.

The driver waited rather than driving off: he was stationary for the entire wait from 08:47:55 until he cancelled at 08:51:55, and he messaged the rider at 08:48 to come out, which shows he genuinely tendered the trip rather than abandoning it.

The rider's own message at 08:49 does not dispute being at the pickup point but asks where the car is, and no message from the rider claims he could not find the location; the driver gave a vehicle description (silver Toyota Altis) to help the rider locate him.

There was no external obstruction preventing the driver from reaching the pickup point: no traffic incidents, no speed-band congestion records, and fair weather with 0.0 mm rain in the trip window, so the shortfall in position cannot be blamed on conditions beyond his control.

weaknesses: NS-1(ii) is not satisfied on the system records: F1 shows the driver's closest approach was 288 m and he never came within 200 m of the pickup point, and F5 shows he was 350 m away when he tapped "I'm Here" and stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds — so the location requirement fails.

F4 is decisive against the client: driver_arrived_at is null, i.e. the platform never recorded him at the pickup point, and F2 places his 4-minute stationary wait 350 m from pickup, not at it. Under the rule that system records beat statements, the driver's written statement F12 ("I waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup") cannot cure this.

Because the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside the pickup radius, NS-2's second limb does not merely produce a refund — it also attracts a flag_account against the driver, and F17 shows a prior upheld no-show dispute, which the rider will use to argue this is a pattern.
The zero-second dwell within 200 m (F5) also means there is no GPS support for a $5 waiting-fee claim, so no offsetting entitlement can be asserted.

points.response: Concede only that the tap happened; it does not help him, because NS-1 requires the tap to be made while at the pickup point, and F5 shows he tapped at 08:48:15 while 350 m away, with F1 confirming his closest approach was 288 m and he never entered 200 m.
The 4 minutes in F2 were spent stationary 350 m from the pickup point (F2), and F5 records 0 seconds inside 200 m, so NS-1(iii)'s 'waited at the pickup point' element is not met by duration alone.

Staying put 350 m away is not tendering the trip at the pickup point: F4 shows the platform never recorded an arrival and F1 shows he never came within 200 m, and his 08:48 'come out' message (F8) invited the rider to a location he had not verified was the pickup point, as her 08:49 reply 'I don't see any car' (F9) confirms.

The rider's message F9 expressly states 'I'm at the pickup point and I don't see any car' — a direct claim she was at the location and could not find him — so D4 misreads the record, and a car description in F8 cannot substitute for being within the 200 m arrival radius.

I agree there was no external obstruction (F13, F14, F15) — which is precisely why the driver's failure to reach the pickup point is unexplained and the fee cannot stand; RD-4 excuses only justified reroutes and is not a defence to a no-show when no arrival within 200 m was ever recorded (F1, F4).

I withdraw nothing, but I clarify: the record contains no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in F8–F12, so the case should be decided automatically under NS-2 rather than escalated on safety grounds.

Conceded: F1 shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 288 m and he never entered the 200 m radius, and F2 places his stationary period at 350 m from pickup, so on the location element of NS-1 the records are against the client.

Conceded: F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 08:48:15 occurred 350 m from the pickup point and that the driver spent 0 s within 200 m afterwards, and F4 confirms no platform-recorded arrival, so NS-1(ii) is not met.

Partially conceded and narrowed: F2 does show 4 min of stationarity, but it was 350 m from the pickup point with 0 s inside the radius (F5), so NS-1(iii)'s "waited at the pickup point" reading is not established by the records; the driver's only surviving point is that he did not abandon the job.

Accepted as far as the driver's wording goes — he offered a car description rather than a location (F8) — but F9 is the rider's own message asking where he was while he sat stationary 350 m away (F2), so nothing in the chat supports the rider's presence independently of her own assertion.

Conceded in substance: the driver's post-trip statement F12 ("waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup") is contradicted by F1, F4 and F5, and under the rule that system records prevail over statements it cannot be used to sustain the $6.61 no-show fee.
Conceded: since NS-1(i)–(iii) are not all satisfied, the $6.61 recorded at F6 (with surge 1.0×, F7) falls to be refunded in full, and the client does not resist that outcome.

The refund follows from NS-2, but the rider's added request that the account be flagged does not: NS-2's flag limb is written for a driver who presses "I'm Here" while GPS shows him outside the pickup point, and F5 does show exactly that, so the client accepts the record but asks that F17's single prior no-show be treated as the only evidence of a pattern, and profile facts may not decide the case (RD-6).
Conceded: F13, F14 and F15 record no speed bands, no incidents and fair weather, so the client cannot and does not claim that road conditions excused the shortfall in position under RD-4.

Agreed and confirmed by the client's own reading of the file: the messages F8, F9, F10 and the statement F12 contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 are not engaged and the case can be decided on the clause-based outcome rather than sent to a person.
